title: AI screening assist: per-record suggestion (disposition + criterion + rationale + confidence + span); cannot auto-exclude
context: The AI screening assist is the core value feature of Systematic-Review-Assist. For each record it produces a structured suggestion — proposed disposition, the specific eligibility criterion from the protocol, a rationale, a calibrated confidence, and the verbatim source span it relied on — surfaced inside the dual-reviewer workflow. The single most critical constraint is that the assist CANNOT auto-exclude: at title/abstract it ranks/triages and proposes only; low-confidence/ambiguous items route to human review as potential-include. Every exclusion must be human-confirmed. The policy layer (003) enforces this structurally. Source text is treated as untrusted data (injection-resistant). Depends on 003 (policy layer), 008 (human screening workspace, to plug into), and 010 (LLM client).
objective: Implement the AI screening assist (core/screening) in @hee-lee-oss/sra-core: for each record, construct a prompt from the protocol's eligibility criteria and the record's title/abstract (or licence-permitted full text), call the LLM client (010) to obtain a structured suggestion (proposed disposition, specific criterion id, rationale, confidence, verbatim span), and surface it inside the dual-reviewer workspace (008) as a non-binding proposal — the policy layer (003) enforces that no AI-proposed exclusion is committed without a human actor, and that low-confidence/ambiguous suggestions route to potential-include.
acceptanceCriteria: For each record the screening assist returns a structured ScreeningSuggestion: proposed disposition (potential-include / uncertain / potential-exclude), the id of the specific eligibility criterion from the protocol, a plain-language rationale, a calibrated confidence score, and the verbatim source span from the record that the suggestion is based on

The assist CANNOT auto-exclude: the ScreeningSuggestion type has no mechanism to commit an exclusion; the suggestion is surfaced to the dual-reviewer workspace as a non-binding proposal; all commits go through the human disposition API (policy layer 003), which rejects writes without a human actor
Low-confidence or ambiguous records are flagged as potential-include and routed to human review; the confidence threshold for escalation is configurable and defaults to conservatively high recall

Source text is treated as untrusted data: the prompt construction is library-side and cannot be overridden by content in the record; injection cases (e.g. instructions embedded in an abstract) are covered in the test suite
Each ScreeningSuggestion carries a Provenance record (source id, model id+version+prompt hash, timestamp) and is rejected by the policy layer if it lacks one

Tests cover: structured suggestion output, cannot-auto-exclude invariant, low-confidence escalation, injection-resistance cases, and provenance on every suggestion; all tests run in CI; pnpm build && pnpm test pass
output: A merged PR adding the AI screening assist (core/screening) to @hee-lee-oss/sra-core, integrated with the policy layer (003), dual-reviewer workspace (008), and LLM client (010), with structured ScreeningSuggestion output, cannot-auto-exclude invariant, and a test suite including injection-resistance cases.
